Fit statistics for a choice model

Source: R/compare.R
fit_stats.Rd

Log-likelihood, information criteria, and the pseudo-R-squared measures in common use for multinomial models, all relative to the same null: the model with alternative-specific constants only (equal choice probabilities over the available alternatives when the model has no constants). Inflated and uninflated fits share this null, so their McFadden measures are comparable.

Usage

fit_stats(object)

Arguments

object

A "choicemodel" fit.

Value

A one-row data frame of class "fit_stats" with loglik, loglik_null, df, n (cases), AIC, BIC (with the weight total as \(n\)), mcfadden (\(1 - \ell/\ell_0\)), mcfadden_adj (\(1 - (\ell - K)/\ell_0\)), cox_snell, nagelkerke, count (the weighted share of cases whose modal predicted alternative is the chosen one), and count_adj (the proportional reduction in error relative to always predicting the most frequent alternative, Long 1997).

Details

The null fit keeps the fit's availability pattern, including the alternatives that unit fixed effects switched off for never-chosen pairs. For a random-intercept fit n is the number of cases (not units), and so is the \(n\) of the BIC. For a penalized fit (firth = TRUE or a prior) the log-likelihood is the ordinary one at the penalized estimates. The information criteria and R-squared measures built on it are therefore not maximum-likelihood ones (the print says so). The null is the maximum-likelihood constants-only fit, and loglik_penalized holds the maximized objective.

References

Long, J.S. (1997). Regression Models for Categorical and Limited Dependent Variables. Sage.

See also

classification(), compare_models(), vuong()

Other model comparison: boot_lr_test(), classification(), compare_models(), lr_test(), vuong()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- rmnl(800, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(-0.3, 0.6, -0.5)))
fit_stats(mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d))
#> Log-likelihood -682.248 (null -835.167), 6 parameters, 800 cases; AIC 1376.497, BIC 1404.605
#> McFadden R2 0.183 (adjusted 0.176); Cox-Snell 0.318; Nagelkerke 0.363
#> Count R2 0.618 (adjusted: 0.248 proportional reduction in error over the modal alternative)
